big: Three AIF categories, three risk levels. Category I backs start-ups and infrastructure. Category II holds private equity and debt with no borrowing for investments. Category III uses complex strategies and leverage.

lines: A fund goes long and short in listed shares and uses derivatives. Which category?

Category III. It uses hedge-fund style trading and may use leverage. Category I covers start-ups, SMEs, social ventures and infrastructure, including angel funds. Category II covers private equity and private debt without leverage beyond day-to-day needs.
